newsitem.title: USA: Deceptive Calif. lawyer to provide immigration aid.
newsitem.headline: Deceptive Calif. lawyer to provide immigration aid.

text.p: The government said on Thursday a Los Angeles immigration lawyer who misled and overcharged thousands of clients around the world had agreed as restitution to provide them with free help to obtain "green cards" for permanent residence in the United States.

The Federal Trade Commission said David Amkraut caused "substantial and unavoidable economic harm" to his clients after they failed to obtain green cards because of delays he caused while he tried to extract $1,000 or more in fees.

An FTC spokeswoman said Amkraut pressured clients who won the first step of a State Department lottery for immigrant visa applications to pay him $1,000 or more before he would pass on information they needed to take the next step quickly.

The lottery is conducted each year to distribute applications for 55,000 immigrant visas. Those who file successful applications may receive immigrant visas, but they must act quickly because there are nearly twice as many lottery winners as there are available visas.
The visas are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis and can be exchanged for permanent residence visas known as "green cards."

Amkraut, who advertised around the world that he could help people obtain permanent residence in the United States, had clients from many countries. After an FTC investigation, he agreed to contact all of his clients for the 1994 and 1995 "green card lotteries" and provide services free of charge for a similar lottery next month, the FTC said.
He also agreed to keep meticulous records to demonstrate to FTC inspectors that he does not deceive his clients again.
